# [TASK] Make Vosk model shutdown safe and guard the embedding dimension

## Task

**`SpeechToTextService.destroy()` can crash the JVM.** `getOrLoadModel()` synchronizes on `this` while loading, but `destroy()` neither synchronizes nor nulls the field. On shutdown with a request in flight, `model.close()` frees the native Vosk handle while another thread is inside `new Recognizer(loadedModel, …)` or `recognizer.acceptWaveForm(…)` using that same pointer — a use-after-free in native code, which takes the JVM down with a SIGSEGV rather than throwing. A rolling restart under load is enough to reach it. Because the field also stays non-null after close, a late-arriving request gets the freed handle back from `getOrLoadModel()`'s fast path.

**The embedding dimension is never checked against the column.** `RecommendationService` persists whatever `embeddingModel.embed` returns into a `vector(768)` column, but the model is env-overridable at runtime (`application.yml` sets it from `${OLLAMA_EMBEDDING_MODEL:nomic-embed-text}`). Pointing it at `mxbai-embed-large` (1024 dims) or `all-minilm` (384) makes every `save()` fail with PostgreSQL's "expected 768 dimensions, not N", surfacing as a 500 on every recommendations request carrying `recentMovies` — and, because `refreshTasteProfile` runs before the `candidates.isEmpty()` check, it fails even when there is nothing to recommend. The 768/model coupling is documented in three comments (`application.yml`, the V2 migration, `UserTasteProfile`) and enforced nowhere.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Shutdown cannot free the Vosk model while a transcription is using it, and a request arriving after shutdown gets a clean error rather than a freed handle
- [x] A mismatched embedding dimension is detected and reported clearly, rather than surfacing as a 500 from the database on every recommendations request
- [x] The failure is caught early enough that a misconfigured embedding model is obvious at startup or first use, not on an unrelated endpoint
- [x] Tests cover the shutdown race and the dimension mismatch
